walkthrough:
Determine the median and quartiles for the $n = 27$ ordered values:
$$\text{Position of Median} = \frac{27 + 1}{2} = 14\text{th value} \implies \text{Median} = 17$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_1 = \frac{27 + 1}{4} = 7\text{th value} \implies Q_1 = 10$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_3 = \frac{3(27 + 1)}{4} = 21\text{st value} \implies Q_3 = 35$$

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Calculate the five-number summary for $n = 27$ ordered data points:
1. Minimum value: $2$
2. Lower quartile ($Q_1$):
$$\text{Rank} = \frac{n + 1}{4} = \frac{28}{4} = 7\text{th value} \implies Q_1 = 10$$
3. Median ($Q_2$):
$$\text{Rank} = \frac{n + 1}{2} = \frac{28}{2} = 14\text{th value} \implies \text{Median} = 17$$
4. Upper quartile ($Q_3$):
$$\text{Rank} = \frac{3(n + 1)}{4} = \frac{84}{4} = 21\text{st value} \implies Q_3 = 35$$
5. Maximum value: $104$

Step 2: Construct the box plot.
- Draw a uniform linear scale covering $0$ to $110$, labeled with medals.
- Place the box boundaries at $Q_1 = 10$ and $Q_3 = 35$.
- Mark the median with a vertical line inside the box at $17$.
- Draw whiskers extending outward to the minimum ($2$) and maximum ($104$), with no line drawn through the box.
